invariants: External email effects carry a stable idempotency key across retries (SHA-256 of the rendered request), and the bounded 24-hour provider retention is documented rather than claimed as exactly-once.

The transport choice is profile-driven configuration (spring.autoconfigure exclude + ConditionalOnProperty), not code paths: production selects Resend explicitly, development and tests keep SMTP/GreenMail.
RESEND_API_KEY lives only in the deployment secret store (Railway preserve()); the properties record fails fast at boot when the key is absent while the provider is resend.
Retry, circuit-breaker, concurrency-limit, and observation annotations ride the Resend send path exactly as the SMTP path carried them.

Resend fallback idempotency fingerprints the exact provider request body (from, to, subject, rendered HTML); a different body cannot reuse a key because Resend rejects same-key/different-payload requests with HTTP 409.

Retryable password-reset events render the immutable expiry instant carried by PasswordResetRequestedEvent as UTC; the delivery key contains a SHA-256 digest of the reset link, never the raw bearer credential.
Email-verification delivery keys likewise use a SHA-256 digest of the verification link; bearer links remain only in the message body.

MESSAGE_RECEIVED email delivery identity includes the individual messageId together with recipient and conversation identity, so separate messages in one conversation do not collapse into one Resend idempotency record.

marketplace.mail.provider defaults to smtp only when absent; a present blank or unsupported value fails startup through the unconditional MailProviderValidationAutoConfiguration before either conditional channel can be skipped silently.
Staging mail is SMTP and does not exercise the production Resend HTTPS transport; operational documentation states this distinction explicitly.
doors: EmailSender.send (the transport-neutral contract) — the notifications path calls the EmailSender INTERFACE directly (EmailNotificationService holds Optional<EmailSender>, never the EmailService SMTP class); the provider configuration selects which implementation binds
EmailServiceAutoConfiguration (SMTP path, provider=smtp or missing) and ResendEmailSenderAutoConfiguration (provider=resend) — mutually exclusive by ConditionalOnProperty
marketplace-app application.yml / application-prod.yml / application-dev.yml / application-test.yml profiles
.railway/railway.ts variable declaration (RESEND_API_KEY preserve) — the deployment-composition door (B6/D10 matrix)
EmailNotificationService / NotificationService tests — the behavioral doors pinned by the existing suites

siblingSearch.family: Outbound HTTP provider transports with secret-store credentials
siblingSearch.result: No second email transport exists (ResendEmailSender is the sole HTTPS provider client in the email family); no other module constructs its own RestClient for email; every other secret-store credential follows the same preserve() + fail-fast properties record pattern (measured on the MAIL_* family in the same file).

siblingSearch.family: Idempotency keys derived from request identity
siblingSearch.result: The payments family uses operation-identity idempotency keys (StableRefundScope precedent, E-08); the Resend key follows the same shape (fingerprint of the frozen request), and the bounded-retention limitation is registered in the PR body rather than hidden.

findings.scenario: A production deployment sends transactional email while Railway blocks outbound SMTP on the plan tier, so the SMTP transport times out (SocketTimeoutException to smtp.resend.com:587) and every notification email leg fails
findings.invariant: Production email rides an HTTPS provider API (Resend) with stable idempotency keys and secret-store credentials; SMTP stays the development/test channel; no secret value ever enters Git
findings.note: Railway's documented SMTP block on the plan tier is the provider-side cause (Railway docs; measured SocketTimeoutException in production logs). Fixed in this PR by the Resend HTTPS transport. Live Railway variable-name read-back on 2026-11-21 confirmed MAIL_FROM exists and RESEND_API_KEY is absent; the MAIL_FROM value and sender-domain verification were not inspected. Merge/deploy remains owner-gated until the owner adds RESEND_API_KEY and verifies the sender identity.
